newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend fall, seen stabilising.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend fall, seen stabilising.

text.p: Polish shares extended Thursday's fall on Friday but analysts said the stronger buying after price-fixing and mixed continous trade signalled the market would flatten out after this week's downward correction.
The market fell 3.3 percent this week after gaining 38 percent since mid December, likely hurt by Wednesday's bearish statement's by U.S. Fed chairman Alan Greenspan, analysts said,

"The market should rebound around Tuesday and then...it will be easier to say if there'll be a continuation of the recent rises in the mid-term or more of a flat trend," said Tomasz Cwintal of Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej (BGZ) brokerage.

The main market's all-share WIG index fell 1.6 percent to 17,543.8 points and turnover fell 13.4 percent to 194.5 million zlotys ($63.6 million) on all three markets. Losers led gainers by 75 to 12 with two stocks flat.
Some analysts said more falls toward 17,000 points were still possible.

Small-cap builder Espebepe, cable maker Kable, food producer Pekpol and builder Remak all fell more than nine percent on Friday, with Espebepe hurt by profit-taking surging on a possible debt write-off deal in mid-March, analysts said.
They said Kable was hurt by Danish NKT Cables' mid-week offer to buy up the firm at a discount to its market price.

Mass privatisation NFI units fell 1.8 percent in a 44.9-million-zloty ($14.7 million) turnover in regular trade and fell 2.1 percent in 29-million-zloty ($9.5 million) continuous trade, where stock trade was mixed and the WIG 20 index inched up 0.1 percent.
